### Fixed
- **`filter_tools` names the servers a sign-in would unlock.** An agent that discovers tools with `filter_tools` — where muster's own `list_tools` description and the platform's agent prompts steer it — never learned that a Connector exists until the person had signed in to it: for a server the session is not connected to, the filter returned no tool and no hint, the agent answered "I have no Slack tool", and the gateway's Connect button, rendered from a `core_auth_login` result, never appeared; only `list_tools` reported `servers_requiring_auth`. `filter_tools` now carries `servers_requiring_auth` too, in `list_tools`' shape (`name`, `status`, `auth_tool`, `tool_prefix`, `family`), narrowed to the servers whose tools the `pattern` could match once they are listed: every pending server without a pattern or under `*slack*`, `slack` alone under `x_slack_*`, none under `core_*` (so `list_core_tools` is unchanged). The toolset does not narrow it — `toolset_requiring_auth` still names the part of the toolset a sign-in would unlock — nor do `query`, `description_filter` and `labels`, which have no text to match before the sign-in; the list is sorted by name, as `list_tools`' now is. An empty catalogue with such a server answers the structured page instead of `No tools available to filter`. The tool's description says so, and the `muster` CLI's filter listing prints the servers as its tool listing does. ([#1351](https://github.com/giantswarm/muster/issues/1351))
